model.nyc_taxi.recon_bronze_silver.raw_code:
-- Bronze -> silver reconciliation, one row per source file month (exam Q3).
-- Row counts: bronze = silver + quarantine, nothing is dropped silently.
-- Amounts: the bronze total is split into what approved metrics keep (valid) and what
-- each status excludes, so every material exclusion is quantified and explained.
with manifest as (
    select distinct on (source_month)
        source_month,
        batch_id,
        row_count_file,
        row_count_bronze
    from {{ source("ops", "ingestion_manifest") }}
    where dataset = 'yellow' and status = 'loaded'
    order by source_month, finished_at desc
),

bronze as (
    select
        source_month,
        count(*) as bronze_rows,
        -- summed as exact decimals (cents), not as floating point
        sum(round(total_amount::numeric, 2)) as bronze_total_amount
    from {{ source("bronze", "yellow_trips_raw") }}
    group by source_month
),

silver as (
    select
        source_month,
        count(*) as silver_rows,
        count(*) filter (where quality_status = 'valid') as valid_rows,
        count(*) filter (where quality_status = 'suspicious') as suspicious_rows,
        count(*) filter (where quality_status = 'invalid') as invalid_rows,
        sum(total_amount) as silver_total_amount,
        sum(total_amount) filter (where quality_status = 'valid') as valid_total_amount,
        sum(total_amount) filter (where quality_status = 'suspicious')
            as suspicious_total_amount,
        sum(total_amount) filter (where quality_status = 'invalid') as invalid_total_amount,
        {% for flag in quality_flag_catalog() -%}
        count(*) filter (where is_{{ flag.code }}) as {{ flag.code }}_rows{{ "," if not loop.last }}
        {% endfor -%}
    from {{ ref("int_trips_flagged") }}
    group by source_month
),

quarantine as (
    select source_month, count(*) as quarantine_rows
    from {{ ref("int_trips_quarantine") }}
    group by source_month
)

select
    m.source_month,
    m.batch_id,
    m.row_count_file as file_rows,
    b.bronze_rows,
    coalesce(s.silver_rows, 0) as silver_rows,
    coalesce(q.quarantine_rows, 0) as quarantine_rows,
    b.bronze_rows - coalesce(s.silver_rows, 0) - coalesce(q.quarantine_rows, 0)
        as unexplained_rows,

    s.valid_rows,
    s.suspicious_rows,
    s.invalid_rows,
    round(100.0 * s.valid_rows / nullif(s.silver_rows, 0), 2) as valid_trip_rate_pct,

    b.bronze_total_amount,
    s.silver_total_amount,
    s.valid_total_amount,
    s.suspicious_total_amount,
    s.invalid_total_amount,
    -- rounding of each amount to cents in staging; expected to be 0.00
    b.bronze_total_amount - s.silver_total_amount as unexplained_amount,

    {% for flag in quality_flag_catalog() -%}
    s.{{ flag.code }}_rows{{ "," if not loop.last }}
    {% endfor -%}
from manifest as m
left join bronze as b on m.source_month = b.source_month
left join silver as s on m.source_month = s.source_month
left join quarantine as q on m.source_month = q.source_month

    d.month_start as pickup_month,
    f.pickup_zone_sk,
    f.dropoff_zone_sk,

    sum(f.total_amount) as sum_total_amount,
    sum(f.fare_amount) as sum_fare_amount,
    sum(f.trip_distance) as sum_trip_distance,
    sum(f.duration_min) as sum_duration_min,
    sum(f.total_amount) filter (where f.trip_distance > 0) as sum_total_amount_with_distance,
    sum(f.trip_distance) filter (where f.trip_distance > 0) as sum_trip_distance_positive
from {{ ref("fct_trip") }} as f
inner join {{ ref("dim_date") }} as d on f.pickup_date_sk = d.date_sk
where f.quality_status = 'valid' and f.pickup_date_sk <> -1
group by 1, 2, 3, 4

model.nyc_taxi.dim_trip_quality.raw_code:
-- Junk dimension: one row per combination of quality flags observed in silver.
-- The key is the hash of the flag list, so it is stable from one build to the next.
--
-- Built from the single quality_flags column (the array holds exactly the raised flags)
-- instead of a DISTINCT over fourteen boolean columns: grouping 10 million rows on one
-- column is far cheaper (the first version took more than two hours on the dev host).
with combinations as (
    select
        quality_flags,
        max(quality_status) as quality_status
    from {{ ref("int_trips_flagged") }}
    group by quality_flags
)

select
    md5(array_to_string(quality_flags, ',')) as trip_quality_sk,
    quality_status,
    array_to_string(quality_flags, ', ') as quality_flags_label,
    cardinality(quality_flags) as flag_count,
    {% for flag in quality_flag_catalog() -%}
    '{{ flag.code }}' = any(quality_flags) as is_{{ flag.code }}{{ "," if not loop.last }}
    {% endfor -%}
from combinations

{#
    Fact table, grain: one completed taxi trip (one row of a TLC file).

    trip_sk is deterministic and readable: YYYYMM of the source file followed by the
    0-based row number in that file on 8 digits. Trip 20250100001204 is row 1204 of
    yellow_tripdata_2025-01.parquet, in every layer and after every re-run.

    Indexes: only source_month (the incremental delete of a month) and a BRIN on pickup_ts.
    Nothing reads single trips from this table in production: aggregates scan it and BI
    and AI read analytics. Three b-tree indexes on 7 million rows (trip_sk, date, zone)
    made a two-month rebuild exceed two hours on the development host.

    Every row of silver is kept, whatever its quality status; approved metrics filter
    on quality_status = 'valid'. Unknown or missing codes point to the Unknown member
    (-1) of their dimension, so every foreign key resolves.
#}
{#
    Every dimension a foreign key of this model points to is declared as a dependency, also
    those whose key is computed here without reading them (time, service period) and the
    role-playing zone views. Two reasons:
    - the relationship tests run with this model (Cosmos, indirect selection "buildable")
      only when every dimension they read is an ancestor of it;
    - rebuilding dim_zone drops dim_pickup_zone and dim_dropoff_zone (DROP ... CASCADE)
      until their own run recreates them; observed on load_2025_04, a test ran in that
      window and failed with "relation does not exist".
#}
-- depends_on: {{ ref("dim_pickup_zone") }}
-- depends_on: {{ ref("dim_dropoff_zone") }}
-- depends_on: {{ ref("dim_time") }}
-- depends_on: {{ ref("dim_service_period") }}
{%- set months = months_to_process() %}

-- trip_quality_sk is computed here (hash of the flag list), so no ref() ties this model
-- to dim_trip_quality. Without this declaration, a new month with new flag combinations
-- was tested against a dimension not yet rebuilt (relationships test failed, 2025-02).
-- depends_on: {{ ref("dim_trip_quality") }}

with trips as (
    select t.*
    from {{ ref("int_trips_flagged") }} as t
    where t.source_month in ({{ date_literals(months) }})
)

select
    -- keys
    (
        to_char(t.source_month, 'YYYYMM')::bigint * 100000000 + t.file_row_number
    ) as trip_sk,
    coalesce(d.date_sk, -1) as pickup_date_sk,
    case
        when t.pickup_ts is null then -1
        else extract(hour from t.pickup_ts)::integer * 100
            + extract(minute from t.pickup_ts)::integer
    end as pickup_time_sk,
    coalesce(pz.zone_sk, -1) as pickup_zone_sk,
    coalesce(dz.zone_sk, -1) as dropoff_zone_sk,
    coalesce(pt.payment_type_sk, -1) as payment_type_sk,
    case
        when t.rate_code_id is null then -2
        else coalesce(rc.rate_code_sk, -1)
    end as rate_code_sk,
    coalesce(v.vendor_sk, -1) as vendor_sk,
    {{ service_period_sk("t.pickup_ts") }} as service_period_sk,
    md5(array_to_string(t.quality_flags, ',')) as trip_quality_sk,

    -- degenerate and technical identifiers (lineage back to the raw file)
    t.source_month,
    t.file_row_number,
    t.batch_id,
    t.source_file,

    -- timestamps (New York local time)
    t.pickup_ts,
    t.dropoff_ts,

    -- measures
    t.passenger_count,
    t.trip_distance,
    t.duration_min,
    t.speed_mph,
    t.fare_amount,
    t.extra_amount,
    t.mta_tax,
    t.tip_amount,
    t.tolls_amount,
    t.improvement_surcharge,
    t.congestion_surcharge,
    t.airport_fee,
    t.cbd_congestion_fee,
    t.total_amount,

    -- attributes used by governed metrics
    (
        coalesce(pz.is_airport, false)
        or coalesce(dz.is_airport, false)
        or coalesce(t.rate_code_id in ({{ var("airport_rate_codes") | join(", ") }}), false)
    ) as is_airport_trip,
    coalesce(pt.is_tip_recorded, false) as is_tip_recorded,
    t.quality_status,
    t.quality_flags,

    current_timestamp as gold_loaded_at
from trips as t
left join {{ ref("dim_date") }} as d on t.pickup_ts::date = d.date_day

        incremental_strategy="delete+insert",

        on_schema_change="fail",
        indexes=[
            {"columns": ["source_month", "file_row_number"], "unique": true},
            {"columns": ["pickup_ts"], "type": "brin"},
        ],
        pre_hook=[
            "set work_mem = '64MB'",
            "set max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 1",
        ],

{#
    Memory of the pre_hook: each sort or hash may use work_mem, in every parallel worker.
    128 MB with two workers contributed to a PostgreSQL backend crash on the 4 GB
    development host while Airflow was running (see docs/evidence/q05).

    Silver trips: one row per bronze row that could be parsed, with derived fields,
    one boolean per quality flag, the flag list and the quality status.

    Nothing is deleted or corrected: approved metrics filter on quality_status = 'valid',
    and every excluded row stays visible with the reason of its exclusion.

    Built month by month (delete+insert on source_month), see macros/months_to_process.sql.
#}
{%- set months = months_to_process() -%}
{%- set tolerance = var("cross_month_tolerance_days") -%}
{%- set natural_key = [
    "vendor_id", "pickup_ts", "dropoff_ts", "pickup_location_id", "dropoff_location_id",
    "trip_distance", "total_amount"
] -%}

with trips as (
    select
        t.*,
        date_trunc('month', t.pickup_ts)::date as pickup_month,

{% macro postgres__get_relations() -%}

  {#
      -- in pg_depend, objid is the dependent, refobjid is the referenced object
      --  > a pg_depend entry indicates that the referenced object cannot be
      --  > dropped without also dropping the dependent object.
  #}

  {%- call statement('relations', fetch_result=True) -%}
    select distinct
        dependent_namespace.nspname as dependent_schema,
        dependent_class.relname as dependent_name,
        referenced_namespace.nspname as referenced_schema,
        referenced_class.relname as referenced_name

    -- Query for views: views are entries in pg_class with an entry in pg_rewrite, but we avoid
    -- a seq scan on pg_rewrite by leveraging the fact there is an "internal" row in pg_depend for
    -- the view...
    from pg_class as dependent_class
    join pg_namespace as dependent_namespace on dependent_namespace.oid = dependent_class.relnamespace
    join pg_depend as dependent_depend on dependent_depend.refobjid = dependent_class.oid
        and dependent_depend.classid = 'pg_rewrite'::regclass
        and dependent_depend.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
        and dependent_depend.deptype = 'i'

    -- ... and via pg_depend (that has a row per column, hence the need for "distinct" above, and
    -- making sure to exclude the internal row to avoid a view appearing to depend on itself)...
    join pg_depend as joining_depend on joining_depend.objid = dependent_depend.objid
        and joining_depend.classid = 'pg_rewrite'::regclass
        and joining_depend.refclassid = 'pg_class'::regclass
        and joining_depend.refobjid != dependent_depend.refobjid

    -- ... we can find the tables they query from in pg_class, but excluding system tables. Note we
    -- don't need need to exclude _dependent_ system tables, because they only query from other
    -- system tables, and so are automatically excluded by excluding _referenced_ system tables
    join pg_class as referenced_class on referenced_class.oid = joining_depend.refobjid
    join pg_namespace as referenced_namespace on referenced_namespace.oid = referenced_class.relnamespace
        and referenced_namespace.nspname != 'information_schema'
        and referenced_namespace.nspname not like 'pg\_%'

    order by
        dependent_schema, dependent_name, referenced_schema, referenced_name;

  {%- endcall -%}

  {{ return(load_result('relations').table) }}
{% endmacro %}

### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.
